page: Amazon Web Services c8gd.48xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processors. It features 192 dedicated physical cores operating at 2.7 GHz with a 1:1 thread-to-core ratio. The system is equipped with 384.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is provided via 11,400 GB of local NVMe SSD instance store volumes, and the instance operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor with a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression all registering in the top 10% of tested systems. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, scoring in the top tier for both cached small-block and uncached large-block read and write operations. However, single-core performance is more moderate, with stress-ng single-core, Geekbench single-core, and single-threaded gzip compression falling into the middle 50% average category.

The hardware configuration and benchmark results make this instance highly suitable for multi-threaded, compute-heavy workloads that require high local storage capacity and fast memory access. It achieves top-tier results in database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput. Conversely, it is less suited for workloads dependent on single-core speed or low-parameter LLM inference, where it exhibits weaker performance. The high density of dedicated ARM64 cores combined with massive local NVMe storage offers a resource-dense profile for distributed databases, software compilation, and parallel data processing.
description: Amazon Web Services c8gd.48xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the ARM64 architecture, featuring 192 dedicated AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 cores running at 2.7 GHz. It is equipped with 384.0 GB of RAM, 11,400 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, and a 50 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark results show top-tier multi-core CPU and memory bandwidth performance, alongside strong database and Redis operations. However, single-core performance remains in the average tier. This instance is highly suited for scale-out multi-threaded workloads, high-throughput static web serving, software compilation, and database applications that benefit from large local NVMe storage and high physical core density.
